title: Book 6 — Erato, Chapter 31
paragraphs: So it happened regarding Histiaeus. Meanwhile the Persian fleet, after wintering near Miletus, when it put to sea again the following year, conquered without difficulty the islands lying near the mainland—Chios, Lesbos, and Tenedos. And whenever they took one of the islands, the barbarians, as each was conquered, swept the inhabitants off it. They do this in the following manner: they extend themselves from the sea on the north to the sea on the south, each man holding the next by the hand, and then pass through the whole island, hunting the people out of it. They took also the Ionian cities on the mainland in the same way, except that they did not sweep off the inhabitants thus, for it was not possible.
